record.title: Title VIII designated-FMU public-authority and standards route
kv: Legal basis
Dodd-Frank Act Title VIII designation and supervisory framework.
When it applies
The operator is an FSOC-designated financial market utility and the relevant statutory supervisory-agency framework applies.
Named firms

Financial Stability Oversight Council (public body); Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (public body); U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (public body); Commodity Futures Trading Commission (public body)
Who can use it

Financial Stability Oversight Council; Statutory supervisory agencies for designated financial market utilities; Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System where the statute assigns the role; Securities and Exchange Commission where the statute assigns the role; Commodity Futures Trading Commission where the statute assigns the role
Conditions

Recover the specific FSOC designation and designated activity. Identify the statutory supervisory agency and applicable risk-management standards. Review the FMU's operative governance, recovery, and participant rules.
The limit
PFMI terminology, technical settlement capability, or market importance does not itself produce an FSOC designation or Title VIII governance obligation.
Evidence
Financial Stability Oversight Council: Title VIII supplies the statutory route for FSOC designation of financial market utilities and activities.
Evidence
Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System: The Board publishes its supervision and regulation role and is a Title VIII supervisory agency in the applicable statutory route.
Evidence

U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission: SEC's Trading and Markets division describes its securities-market regulatory role; Exchange Act section 19 provides a Commission process for SRO proposed rule changes.
Evidence
Commodity Futures Trading Commission: The Commodity Exchange Act provides CFTC designation/registration routes for defined derivatives-market functions.
